'''Joshua N. Goldberg''' (May 30, 1925 – October 5, 2020) was an American physicist and educator who was particularly noted for his research on [[general relativity]].<ref name=Post-Standard>{{cite news |title=Joshua Goldberg |work=Syracuse Post-Standard |date=October 22, 2020 |url=https://obits.syracuse.com/obituaries/syracuse/obituary.aspx?n=joshua-goldberg&pid=196982650&fhid=3716}}</ref><ref name=APS /><ref name=GRG />

==Early life and education==
Goldberg was born in [[Rochester, New York|Rochester]], New York, and received a bachelor's degree from the [[University of Rochester]] in 1947. He received a doctorate in physics from [[Syracuse University]] in 1952.<ref>{{cite thesis |type=PhD |date=1952 |last1=Goldberg |first1=Joshua N. |title=Equations of motion in a covariant field theory |publisher=Syracuse University |publication-place= Syracuse, NY |oclc=862812419 |language=English}}</ref> His thesis advisor was [[Peter Bergmann]].

==Career==
From 1952–1956 Goldberg was a research scientist at the [[Armour Research Foundation]]. He then worked at the Aerospace Research Laboratory at [[Wright Patterson Air Force Base]], where over seven years he built a research group working on relativity. In 1963 Goldberg became a professor of physics at Syracuse University, where he was an emeritus professor of physics.<ref name=CV />

Goldberg is known for his research in [[general relativity]], where he has written 61 papers.<ref name=CV>{{cite web |title=Josh Goldberg |url=http://asfaculty.syr.edu/pages/phy/_CVs/JNGoldbergCV-1995_1.pdf |work=Curriculum Vitae |publisher=Syracuse University |accessdate=August 30, 2017 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170827090734/http://asfaculty.syr.edu/pages/phy/_CVs/JNGoldbergCV-1995_1.pdf |archivedate=2017-08-27}}</ref> He and [[Rainer K. Sachs]] published the [[Goldberg-Sachs Theorem]] in 1962. Along with Bergmann, Goldberg introduced a new derivation of the laws of motion of rigid bodies according to the rigorous approach that they had developed.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=e8F38Pu0YgEC&pg=PA12 |title=The Noether Theorems: Invariance and Conservation Laws in the Twentieth Century |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|year=2010 |author1=E. Schwarzbach, Bertram |author2=Kosmann-Schwarzbach, Yvette |edition=illustrated |isbn=978-0-387878683 |accessdate=September 11, 2014}}</ref>

Goldberg was elected a Fellow of the American Physical Society in 1972.<ref name=APS>{{cite web |title=APS Fellow Archive |publisher=American Physical Society |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=G&year=2016&unit_id=&institution=}}</ref> In 2011, Goldberg's research career was honored by a special issue of the journal ''[[General Relativity and Gravitation]]''.<ref name=GRG>{{cite journal |editor1-first=E. N. |editor1-last=Glass |editor2-first=D. C. |editor2-last=Robinson |title=Physics, Gravity, and the Work of Joshua N. Goldberg |journal=General Relativity and Gravitation |volume=43 |issue=12 |date=December 2011 |doi=10.1007/s10714-011-1264-9|doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Death==
Goldberg died in Madison, Wisconsin, on October 5, 2020, at the age of 95.<ref name=Post-Standard /><ref name="SU_News_obit">{{cite news |last1=Bernardi |first1=Dan |title=Remembering Joshua Goldberg, Professor Emeritus of Physics in the College of Arts and Sciences |url=https://news.syr.edu/blog/2020/10/15/remembering-joshua-goldberg-professor-emeritus-of-physics-in-the-college-of-arts-and-sciences/ |accessdate=15 October 2020 |work=SU News |date=October 15, 2020}}</ref>
